title: Ask, then ask again: nested input decisions
idea: An answer can gate a second question. Combine input() with nested if to ask a follow-up only when it is relevant. Predict the path.

exercises.prompt: Sometimes the second question only matters depending on the first answer. That calls for...
options: a nested if, with the follow-up inside the first branch
exercises.explanation: Gate the follow-up inside the branch it belongs to - the nesting idea, now driven by typed answers.
"yes" enters the outer branch and triggers the seat question; "vip" matches, so "VIP lounge" prints.

exercises.prompt: Same code, the user types yes then regular. What prints?
exercises.explanation: "yes" asks the seat question; "regular" is not "vip", so the inner else prints "Main hall".

exercises.prompt: Same code, the user types no. What prints, and is the seat question asked?
options: No entry - and the seat question is never asked
Main hall - after asking the seat
exercises.explanation: "no" fails the outer test, so the whole inner block (including the second input) is skipped. Only "No entry" prints.

exercises.prompt: A second input() inside the if is only reached when the outer condition is true.
exercises.explanation: Yes - it lives inside the outer branch, so the follow-up question is asked only when it is relevant.

exercises.prompt: Why put the seat question INSIDE the ticket check?
options: There is no point asking about a seat if they have no ticket
exercises.explanation: The follow-up only makes sense after the first answer. Nesting asks it exactly when it matters - no wasted questions.

exercises.prompt: Build: ask if they want dessert; if "yes", ask which and print it; if not, print "Just the bill".
exercises.explanation: The second question (which dessert) is nested inside the yes branch, so it is only asked if they want dessert.

exercises.prompt: For that dessert code, the user types yes then cake. What prints?
exercises.explanation: "yes" triggers the which-dessert question; pick holds "cake", so "Serving " + pick is "Serving cake".

options: input() plus nested if - asking a follow-up only when relevant
exercises.explanation: You are gating a second input behind the first answer - interactive nesting, the full decision toolkit at work.

options: A typed answer can control whether a follow-up question is even asked
exercises.explanation: Nesting input() inside a branch makes conversations feel natural - the program asks what matters, when it matters.
